query: For high-entropy alloys in demanding engineering applications, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment that could falsify it?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Zr to a high-entropy alloy can improve its resistance to thermally induced toughness loss by enhancing solid solution strengthening and grain refinement.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy with a single phase structure
generation.conditions: High temperature and high strain rate
generation.structural_mediator: Grain refinement and solid solution strengthening
generation.mechanism: Enhanced dislocation activity and deformation-induced nano-twinning
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved resistance to thermally induced toughness loss
generation.boundary: Temperature and strain rate limits beyond which the alloy's properties degrade
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Zr required for optimal performance and the potential effects of other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of high-entropy alloys with and without Zr addition under high temperature and high strain rate conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with Zr addition does not show improved resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, the hypothesis is falsified.

Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility). Selective Laser Melting (SLM) Additively Manufactured CoCrFeNiMn High-Entropy Alloy: Process Optimization, Microscale Mechanical Mechanism, and High-Cycle Fatigue Behavior

Abstract: AbstractThe equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy (HEA) possesses excellent properties including exceptional strength–ductility synergy, high corrosion resistance, and good thermal stability. Selective laser melting (SLM) additive manufacturing facilitates the convenient fabrication of the CoCrFeNiMn HEA parts with complex geometries. Here, the SLM process optimization was conducted to achieve a high relative density of as-built CoCrFeNiMn HEA bulks. The mechanisms of process-induced defects and process control were elucidated. The microscale mechanical behaviors were analyzed through in situ scanning electron microscopy observation during the compression tests on micro-pillars of the as-built HEA. The stress–strain characteristics by repeated slip and mechanism of “dislocation avalanche” during the compression of micro-pillars were discussed.
